A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DEER-3D, with matching authors, core pipeline and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original grounding and scene-understanding experiments, augmentation and QA ablations, iterative refinement results, and instruction-distribution analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds an LL3DA evaluation, human assessments of pipeline quality, runtime measurements and qualitative grounding examples.

M1.justification: The decomposition, candidate checking, Clone–Replace–Modify operations, QA generation and iterative training remain. v2 newly specifies keyword/target-label filtering, conservative no-edit decisions and geometric sanity checks, but does not establish whether these change the implemented procedure or disclose previously omitted details.

E1.justification: Both versions cover ScanRefer, Multi3DRefer, Scan2Cap, ScanQA, SQA3D and BEACON-3D. The LL3DA experiment changes the backbone, while the human audits and qualitative examples examine the existing pipeline and grounding coverage; no new dataset, domain or external test scenario is established.

E2.justification: v2 adds LL3DA as a comparator in the ScanRefer refinement experiment (Table 4), whereas v1 reports it only in scene-understanding comparisons. Conversely, 3D-VisTA is removed from the ScanRefer subset comparison (v1 Table 7 versus v2 Tables 2 and 10), although retained in Table 1.

E3.justification: v2 adds manual evaluation protocols for 100 decomposed instructions, 200 predicate classifications and 60 edited scenes (Appendix A.3), plus ScanRefer testing with the scene-level LL3DA backbone. These substantially extend the evaluation design. The existing grounding metrics, augmentation counts, five-epoch training schedule and optimizer settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds cross-backbone validation, human analyses of decomposition/classification reliability and scene plausibility, computational-overhead analysis, and two qualitative cases. It removes the QA-type and explanation ablation from v1 Table 2 and its discussion; these are not relocated to the appendix. Existing scaling, edit-strategy, text-only and third-round analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both retain the error bars in Figure 4(c), without adding their definition, repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new human-evaluation sample sizes and percentages do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: DEER-3D's Table 1 scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds LL3DA ScanRefer results (25.7/20.8 baseline versus 29.2/25.2 refined), 85% predicate agreement, 87% scene plausibility, runtime measurements and qualitative outcomes. Inst3D-LLM's Table 1 Multi3DRefer F1@0.5 changes from 53.5 to 45.5. Random-Text and DEER-3D+Text-Aug ScanRefer Acc@0.25 change from 56.1/56.6 to 55.8/56.4. The QA-ablation results and 3D-VisTA subset entries are removed.

T1.justification: The prediction, translation, rotation and CIELAB color-selection formulas remain mathematically equivalent; replacing ground-truth notation with target notation does not change them. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains error-driven counterfactual scene editing for improved grounding. v2 narrows the abstract's consistent-improvement statement from all evaluated datasets to grounding datasets, and changes the introduction's summarized gains from 4–5% to 4–6%.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking retained subset gains to same-category object disambiguation and new qualitative examples to transfer beyond edited spatial predicates. It clarifies the limits of model self-explanation and physical-plausibility heuristics, while removing the interpretation that comparative explanations improve performance alongside the deleted QA ablation. Appendix C's broader limitations remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands implementation disclosure: Appendix A.1 identifies Uni3D, DINOv2, projection MLPs and Vicuna-7B-v1.5; Sections 3.3–3.4 and Appendix A.3 detail predicate filtering and editing constraints. Appendix B.2 adds training-time and overhead measurements. Existing hyperparameters, EMA training and the code-access address are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for Vicuna, DINOv2 and Uni3D, and removes RL4F, LLMRefine and the work on locating versus correcting reasoning errors. Related work more explicitly emphasizes language–geometry alignment, while retaining the same broad positioning against textual augmentation and general-purpose scene editing.

P1.justification: v2 revises portions of the abstract, motivation, related work and diagnostic explanation, consolidates experimental setup, and reorganizes appendix subsections. Terminology shifts toward predicate-guided intervention and target objects, but the overall narrative sequence and much of the original prose remain.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column layout to a narrow single-column format, extensively resizing and reflowing figures and tables. v2 adds LL3DA and predicate-vocabulary tables and Figure 7, removes the QA-ablation table, and redisplays the subset comparisons in both the main text and appendix.

improvement.justification: The LL3DA experiment and human quality checks add useful evidence about generality and pipeline reliability, while the expanded implementation and runtime disclosures improve transparency. However, removing v1's QA-type ablation weakens support for the supervision design, and the principal benchmark results and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged. The additions support a limited net improvement.
